biography:
Everton Braz, a name synonymous with both brilliance and frustration in the Brazilian racing scene, hails from the sun-drenched streets of Rio de Janeiro. Growing up amidst the roar of engines and the fervent passion of local karting circuits, Braz's destiny was sealed early. His father, a mechanic with a deep love for motorsport, introduced him to the world of speed at a tender age. One sweltering afternoon, while tinkering with his father's old go-kart, young Everton spontaneously fired it up and tore around their neighborhood, dodging bewildered pedestrians and barking dogs. That reckless joy solidified his path. 

Braz clawed his way through the ranks, showcasing raw talent and an undeniable flair for the dramatic. His early years with Uno Classic B were marked by flashes of brilliance interspersed with inexplicable errors. He'd pull off audacious overtakes one lap, then spin out unforced the next. This inconsistency has plagued his career. Despite possessing undeniable skill, Braz has never quite reached his full potential. He remains a veteran presence in the paddock, a reminder of both the allure and the cruelty of motorsport. 

Now at 38, Everton is facing the twilight of his career. While some whisper that he’s past his prime, others believe that a change of scenery or a stroke of luck could reignite the spark. He continues to compete, driven by a stubborn refusal to concede defeat and a deep-seated love for the thrill of the race. His continued presence in the sport serves as a beacon of hope for young, upcoming drivers; a testament to the unwavering spirit required to chase the checkered flag.
drivingStyle: Braz is known for his aggressive, almost reckless driving style. He attacks corners with a ferocity that often leaves spectators breathless. While undeniably exciting, this approach frequently leads to tire degradation and costly mistakes. He struggles to manage pressure, often cracking under intense scrutiny, resulting in unforced errors in crucial moments. However, when he's 'on,' Braz is a force to be reckoned with, capable of pulling off daring overtakes and defending his position with unwavering determination.

careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian National Championship in 2010 after a stunning final-lap overtake, cementing his status as a national hero for a fleeting moment.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2015 Sao Paulo Grand Prix with only two laps remaining, a mistake that cost him a potential career-defining victory.
